title: Relative clauses and comparisons
intro: Join ideas smoothly with who, which, that, whose and where, use commas correctly, and compare people, places and plans like a fluent speaker.
introBn: who, which, whose, where দিয়ে বাক্য জোড়া লাগানো, কমার সঠিক ব্যবহার, আর তুলনা করার নিয়ম শিখুন।

units.title: Who, which, that, whose, where
units.idea: A relative clause adds information about a noun. Use who for people, which for things, that for either (in defining clauses), whose for possession and where for places.
units.ideaBn: relative clause দিয়ে noun সম্পর্কে তথ্য যোগ হয়। মানুষ = who, জিনিস = which, দুটোই = that, যার = whose, যেখানে = where।

formula.name: People / things
formula.pos: the client who called · the laptop which / that I bought

formula.name: Possession / place
formula.pos: the colleague whose father is ill · the café where we met

uses.ex: The man who interviewed me was very kind.
The phone that I bought last week has stopped working.
Rafi has a flatmate whose brother works at a bank.
This is the restaurant where we had our office party.

uses.rule: Drop who/which/that when it is the object.
uses.bn: object হলে who/that বাদ দেওয়া যায়।
uses.ex: The report (that) you sent is excellent.

traps.wrong: The man which called you is here.
traps.right: The man who called you is here.

traps.wrong: The house where I live in is small.
traps.right: The house where I live is small. / The house I live in is small.

traps.wrong: This is the book which I bought it.
traps.right: This is the book which I bought.

drills.s: The printer ___ we ordered hasn't arrived.
I share a flat with a guy ___ sister is a doctor.
Rajshahi is the city ___ I grew up.

o: The client which complained has called again.
The client who complained has called again.
The client whose complained has called again.
The client who he complained has called again.
drills.a: The client who complained has called again.

drills.q: যে মেয়েটা আমার পাশে বসে, সে খুব ভালো ডিজাইনার।
o: The girl who sits next to me is a very good designer.
The girl which sits next to me is a very good designer.
The girl who she sits next to me is a very good designer.
The girl sits next to me she is a very good designer.
drills.a: The girl who sits next to me is a very good designer.

drills.s: That's the meeting room ___ we had the interview in.
drills.x: Object relative can be dropped; 'where' would clash with 'in'.

o: This is the app which I told you about it.
This is the app I told you about.
This is the app where I told you about.
This is the app who I told you about.
drills.a: This is the app I told you about.
drills.x: Object pronoun dropped, preposition at the end.

units.title: Defining vs non-defining clauses
units.idea: A defining clause tells us which one and has no commas. A non-defining clause adds extra information between commas; it uses who or which, never that, and you cannot drop the relative word.
units.ideaBn: defining clause বলে দেয় কোনটা (কমা নেই)। non-defining clause অতিরিক্ত তথ্য দেয়, দুই পাশে কমা থাকে, আর সেখানে that বসে না।

formula.name: Defining
formula.pos: My brother who lives in London is a doctor. (I have more than one brother.)

formula.name: Non-defining
formula.pos: My brother, who lives in London, is a doctor. (I have one brother.)

formula.name: Which for a whole idea
formula.pos: , which: He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.

uses.rule: Names and unique people always take non-defining clauses.
uses.bn: নাম বা একমাত্র ব্যক্তির পরে কমা।
uses.ex: Mr Hasan, who joined last year, leads the team.
Dhaka, which is very crowded, is growing fast.
The staff who work weekends get extra pay.

uses.rule: , which can refer to a whole sentence.
uses.ex: The flight was cancelled, which meant another night in Dubai.
The employees, who were late, were warned. (all were late)

traps.wrong: My mother, that is a teacher, lives in Bogura.
traps.right: My mother, who is a teacher, lives in Bogura.

traps.wrong: Dhaka which is the capital is very busy.
traps.right: Dhaka, which is the capital, is very busy.
traps.why: A name needs commas around extra information.

traps.wrong: He was late again, that annoyed the boss.
traps.right: He was late again, which annoyed the boss.

drills.s: Our CEO, ___ studied at BUET, is an engineer.
Sylhet, ___ is famous for tea, is beautiful in winter.
The client paid early, ___ was a nice surprise.
My father, ___ is retired, now grows vegetables.

o: Rafi's office, that is in Gulshan, is very modern.
Rafi's office, which is in Gulshan, is very modern.
Rafi's office which is in Gulshan, is very modern.
Rafi's office, where is in Gulshan, is very modern.
drills.a: Rafi's office, which is in Gulshan, is very modern.

drills.q: আমার একমাত্র বোন, যে কানাডায় থাকে, আগামী মাসে আসছে।
o: My only sister, who lives in Canada, is coming next month.
My only sister who lives in Canada is coming next month.
My only sister, that lives in Canada, is coming next month.
My only sister, which lives in Canada, is coming next month.
drills.a: My only sister, who lives in Canada, is coming next month.

drills.q: Which sentence means only some staff got a bonus?
o: The staff, who met the target, got a bonus.
The staff who met the target got a bonus.
The staff, that met the target, got a bonus.
The staff which met the target got a bonus.
drills.a: The staff who met the target got a bonus.
drills.x: Defining: only those who met it.

drills.s: The server went down at 3 pm, ___ meant we lost two hours.

units.title: Comparisons: -er, most, as...as, the more
units.idea: Short adjectives add -er / -est; longer ones use more / most. Use as + adjective + as for equality, not as...as for less, and 'the + comparative, the + comparative' to show two things changing together.
units.ideaBn: ছোট adjective-এ -er/-est, বড়টায় more/most। সমান বোঝাতে as...as। 'যত বেশি... তত বেশি' = the more..., the more...।

formula.name: Comparative / superlative
formula.pos: cheap → cheaper → the cheapest · expensive → more expensive → the most expensive

formula.name: Equality
formula.pos: as + adjective + as: as busy as Dhaka · not as fast as

formula.name: Double comparative
formula.pos: The sooner we start, the sooner we finish.

uses.rule: Never double: more better is wrong.

uses.ex: It's the busiest road in the city.
The bus is not as fast as the metro.
The more you practise, the more confident you become.

traps.wrong: More you work, more you earn.
traps.right: The more you work, the more you earn.

drills.s: Living in Dhaka is more expensive ___ living in Rajshahi.
This is ___ road in the whole city.
The bus isn't as fast ___ the metro rail.
The earlier you start, ___ better the result.

o: Her presentation was more better than mine.
Her presentation was better than mine.
Her presentation was more good than mine.
Her presentation was better from mine.
drills.a: Her presentation was better than mine.

drills.q: ঢাকায় যত বেশি থাকি, তত বেশি ভালো লাগে।
o: The longer I live in Dhaka, the more I like it.
More I live in Dhaka, more I like it.
The longer I live in Dhaka, more I like it.
Longer I live in Dhaka, the more I like it.
drills.a: The longer I live in Dhaka, the more I like it.

drills.s: His new job is ___ his old one: same salary, same hours.
This is the ___ week I've had all year.

mastery.s: I work with someone ___ husband is a pilot.
Cox's Bazar, ___ has the longest natural sea beach, is always busy.
That's the café ___ I first met my wife.

o: Our manager, that is from Khulna, is very calm.
Our manager, who is from Khulna, is very calm.
Our manager who is from Khulna, is very calm.
Our manager, which is from Khulna, is very calm.
mastery.a: Our manager, who is from Khulna, is very calm.

mastery.q: এটা আমার দেখা সবচেয়ে সুন্দর জায়গা।
o: This is the most beautiful place I have ever seen.
This is the beautifulest place I have ever seen.
This is more beautiful place I have ever seen.
This is the most beautiful place which I have ever seen it.
mastery.a: This is the most beautiful place I have ever seen.

mastery.s: The second offer is much ___ than the first.
The more you buy, the ___ you pay per unit.

o: The laptop I bought it is very slow.
The laptop I bought is very slow.
The laptop who I bought is very slow.
The laptop where I bought is very slow.
mastery.a: The laptop I bought is very slow.

decide.yes: Use who (or that in a defining clause).
decide.no: Thing: which / that. Place: where. Possession: whose.

decide.q: Is the information extra, about a name or the only one?
decide.yes: Put it between commas and use who / which, never that.
decide.no: No commas; that is fine and can often be dropped if it is the object.
